title: A snapshot id for a scenario's inputs

blocks.text: A water utility (a fictional one) keeps its planning scenarios as JSON-ready dictionaries: budgets, floors, the projects a planner forced in or out, and the solver settings. It wants a **snapshot id** for each scenario, so that two runs can be compared by their ids, and a short answer to "what is different between these two scenarios?".

items: `snapshot_id(inputs)`: the sha256 hex digest of one **canonical text** of the inputs, encoded as UTF-8. The canonical text is the inputs written as JSON with every dictionary's keys sorted and no spaces (separators `","` and `":"`), and with the lists under `force_in` and `force_out` sorted, because they are sets of project ids. Two scenarios that differ only in the order their dictionaries were built, or the order of those id lists, must get the same id; any other change must give a different one.
`changed_fields(a, b)`: the sorted top-level field names whose values differ between two scenarios, by the same canonical rules. A field that only one of them has is a change.

blocks.text: Two details of the canonical text. Only the top-level `force_in` and `force_out` lists are sorted; a list of that name nested inside another field (say `settings`) is written in the order it has. And the text is `json.dumps`'s output with its default `ensure_ascii=True`, so a character outside ASCII is written as an escape: a region named `"Côte"` appears as `"C\u00f4te"`. The UTF-8 encoding is then applied to that text.

Before you code, write the canonical text of `{"force_in": ["W2", "W1"], "budget": {"2028": 950, "2027": 900}}` by hand. The tests compare your id with the digest of texts written out by hand. About ten lines; Python's `json` and `hashlib` do the work.

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from snapshot import changed_fields, snapshot_id

a = {"budget": {"2031": 640}, "force_in": ["P9", "P2"], "force_out": ["P5"], "settings": {"gap": 0.0}}
b = {"settings": {"gap": 0.0}, "force_out": ["P5"], "force_in": ["P2", "P9"], "budget": {"2031": 640}}
c = {**a, "budget": {"2031": 600}, "force_out": []}

print("id of a:", snapshot_id(a))
print("id of b:", snapshot_id(b))
print("id of c:", snapshot_id(c))
print("fields changed a -> c:", changed_fields(a, c))

cases.says: the id is the sha256 of the inputs' canonical text, and a changed value changes it
the fields whose values differ are listed, sorted, and equal inputs list none
inputs built in another key order have the same id
the order of a list of overridden projects changes neither the id nor the diff
a field present in one scenario only is a changed field
a name with a character outside ASCII is written as a JSON escape before hashing

origin.section: A Scenario Is a Copy With Its Own Snapshot, Never an Edit of Another Scenario

concepts: a scenario's id is a hash of its canonical inputs, settings included, so equal inputs share an id
